transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Bell (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood CSM), Sana Kapoor (EdenWare Head of Product), Luis Ortega (ML Lead), Maya Patel (Security), Tom Reynolds (Eng Manager), Jin Soo (Data Analyst)

Summary: quick stability deep-dive on current pilot results, focused on recent regression on mid-tail prompts, guardrail false-positive spike, and an action plan to run a 24h stability sweep with KV prefix caching and adjusted scoring thresholds. Decide rollback drill timing and share security artifacts.

Topics:
- Recent perf/regression signal (p95/p99 increase on 3 prompt families)
- Scoring drift vs training baseline (F1 drop on edge cases)
- Guardrail FP increase after prompt tuning
- KV/prefix caching and batching tradeoffs
- Security and KMS integration questions
- Next steps and owners

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. we'll kick off the weekly pov check — sorry P O C, weekly sync. let's do a quick status and then jump into the regression signals Luis flagged.
[00:12] Sana Kapoor: thanks, Avery. quick note — we're short-staffed on product this week, i'll try to keep my updates brief.
[00:18] Luis Ortega: yeah hi all. so high level, last run we saw a p95 jump from 420ms to roughly 780ms on a subset of mid-length prompts, and the scorecard shows F1 drop from 0.89 to 0.81 on the customer intent set.
[00:35] Marcus Bell: gotcha. when you say "mid-length" do you mean the 150-300 token bucket? or the 300-512?
[00:42] Luis Ortega: mostly 180-260 tokens, so yeah the 150-300 bucket. it's consistent across the 3 prompt families in the set we sent over.
[00:49] Avery Chen: ok that aligns with what we saw in the telemetry — interestingly p50 is fine, it's the tail that moved. that often points to KV cache misses or a batching contention issue.
[01:02] Tom Reynolds: to add, we did increase our client-side max_concurrent to 8 last week for throughput tests. could be interacting with the runtime.
[01:10] Marcus Bell: that could absolutely explain it — when concurrency increases you can get more cold KV cache lookups per model shard. we'll run a prefix KV test. i want to check the cache hit ratio during that time span.
[01:21] [crosstalk]
[01:22] Maya Patel: sorry to jump in — from security side, the regression coincided with our attempt to rotate keys in staging but not prod, not sure if that matters. we do require HSM-backed KMS in prod per our compliance.
[01:33] Avery Chen: good flag, maya. to be clear Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSMs; we'll get the integration docs. nina will follow up with the SOC2 artifact pack.
[01:44] Nina Park: yep i'll send the compliance bundle after the call.
[01:47] Luis Ortega: on the scoring side, we're seeing guardrail false-positives up 3x after the latest prompt surgery. the safety classifier is catching more edge cases as violative — some look like false alarms.
[01:58] Marcus Bell: hmm, is that the rule-based front-end or the LLM-based guardrail?
[02:02] Luis Ortega: it's the LLM-based detector we deployed as a secondary check, the one we tuned to be conservative.
[02:08] Avery Chen: that's consistent: tuning for recall to avoid misses sometimes spikes FP. we usually suggest a curve: lower the detector threshold slightly for those specific prompt families and then apply a more restrictive post-filter for high-risk intents.
[02:21] Sana Kapoor: can you give a concrete example? like what numbers are we talking about for thresholds?
[02:26] Marcus Bell: sure. if your detector probability threshold is 0.72 and you're seeing FPs, we recommend trying 0.66 for family-B prompts where the business cost of a FP is low, while keeping 0.78 for finance/legal-related prompts. and pair that with a second rule that checks entities.
[02:44] Jin Soo: just to note, the dataset has more abbreviations and product ids that might be confusing the model, e.g., EDN-42 vs "Edn forty-two" — transcription artifacts on our side probably.
[02:55] Marcus Bell: yeah those tokenization edge cases do cause odd logits. a simple preprocessor normalizing product ids helps.
[03:04] Tom Reynolds: question on the rollback plan: if we flip to the previous prompt templates, what's the expected perf delta? are we talking 10% cost increase?
[03:12] Avery Chen: in our tests rollback to prior templates regains the earlier F1 (~0.88) and reduces p95 by about 30-35%, cost delta depends on batching but typically a 7-12% increase because you lose some caching opportunities. we'll quantify in the 24h run.
[03:27] Luis Ortega: ok i want the 24h run. we need to be confident before we expand to canary.
[03:31] Marcus Bell: understood. i'll spin up a run with: KV prefix caching enabled, concurrent_clients=4, batch_target=8, and we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token-cost delta.
[03:43] Maya Patel: and please include encryption-in-flight metrics and KMS rotations in the log, we want to correlate with the earlier anomaly.
[03:51] Marcus Bell: yep will do. we'll also export the trace IDs so you can map to your infra logs.
[03:57] [15:00 -> 15:10ish small side discussion about scheduling — omitted for brevity]
[04:10] Avery Chen: shifting to scoring drift — Luis, can you walk us through a couple of the failing examples?
[04:15] Luis Ortega: sure, example one: prompt A asked for cancellation steps but the model hallucinated policy details leading to false positive content classification. the prompt had been shortened to reduce tokens earlier.
[04:26] Marcus Bell: that suggests prompt surgery removed important guardrail context. when you prune prompts for latency you can remove disambiguating phrases.
[04:33] Jin Soo: we did prune examples to reduce latency; maybe over-pruned. i'll share the pre- and post- prompt diffs.
[04:39] Sana Kapoor: what's our acceptable alpha on hallucination? we proposed tolerating some hallucination on non-sensitive topics but not on policy/legal.
[04:47] Avery Chen: we typically classify tolerances by intent-sensitivity matrix — category low/medium/high. for high sensitivity (policy/legal/account), tolerance is near zero for hallucinations; for low-sensitivity it's looser. we'll help codify that for your success criteria doc.
[05:01] Maya Patel: also need audit logs for every token decision — can Redwood provide per-request token trace with model version and prompt hash?
[05:09] Marcus Bell: yes, we produce request-level traces including model hash, prompt hash, kv-cache-hit flag, and execution path. retention is configurable.
[05:16] Maya Patel: retention TTL is important — we need 2y retention for audit trails, is that supported in the private deployment?
[05:23] Avery Chen: in Private yes; Hosted can do extended retention as an add-on but Private gives you full control over retention and KMS.
[05:30] Tom Reynolds: we're leaning private for prod because of the KMS/HSM requirement and data residency. question — what's the deployment lift? weeks? months?
[05:38] Avery Chen: Private with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS usually takes 6-10 weeks for most customers. if you already have on-prem infra it can be faster. Dedicated reserved capacity is a middle ground if you want faster time-to-prod.
[05:52] Sana Kapoor: timeline wise, we're targetting internal pilot sign-off by end of June. does that line up with a 6-10 week private deploy?
[05:59] Avery Chen: it's tight for private to be fully done by end of June if we start mid-May, but Dedicated or Hosted with KMS vault could meet the timeline. we'll surface options and a timeline chart.
[06:12] Marcus Bell: back to the FP spike — do you have a rollback threshold? i.e., at what FP rate do we automatically revert?
[06:18] Luis Ortega: our product team recommended a human-in-the-loop revert for now, but auto-revert if customer visible error rate > 2% for 30m.
[06:27] Marcus Bell: ok we'll craft a canary policy with those thresholds and automatic flagging, plus manual rollback button.
[06:33] [07:00] Jin Soo: small thing — our scoring rubric weights precision higher than recall at 0.6/0.4; maybe we should tweak for these families.
[07:41] Marcus Bell: that's an easy lever: bump precision weight to 0.7 for finance/legal. for exploratory prompts keep 0.55 precision. we'll add that to the scorecard suggestion.
[07:55] Avery Chen: nina, can you confirm you'll share the scorecard template after?
[07:58] Nina Park: yep sharing within 24h.
[08:01] Sana Kapoor: what about burst capacity? last week we saw an end-of-month spike in traffic and latency climbed — is burst scaling on by default?
[08:10] Marcus Bell: yes, Redwood Dedicated/Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity; hosted has policies too. the tradeoff is that burst warms new instances which can momentarily increase p95. we can recommend a scheduled warm-up before predictable spikes.
[08:24] Tom Reynolds: so for the upcoming marketing push we'll schedule a warm-up window?
[08:28] Avery Chen: absolutely — we can script a synthetic warm-up ramp that primes the KV caches and model weights.
[08:35] Maya Patel: compliance question — SSO/SAML provisioning and RBAC, do you integrate with Azure AD + SCIM?
[08:42] Nina Park: yes we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC in Private and as an enterprise add-on for Hosted.
[08:52] [09:00] (short pause while docs shared)
[09:10] Marcus Bell: ok call to the tech next steps: 24h stability run, collect traces, compare pre/post prompt surgery, try threshold adjustments on guardrail, and run a KV-prefix-cache variant. i'll own the run and share spreadsheet.
[09:26] Jin Soo: i'll prepare the final prompt-set (2k examples) and current rubric, will send by Monday.
[09:33] Sana Kapoor: legal and security will review the SOC2 pack. maya will coordinate with you guys.
[09:38] Maya Patel: yes, i'll review and ping any missing artifacts.
[09:42] Avery Chen: good. let's set the rollback drill — propose 2026-05-26 14:00 UTC for a 45m session?
[09:49] Tom Reynolds: works for eng.
[09:51] Sana Kapoor: works for product.
[09:52] Marcus Bell: locking that in — i'll send calendar invite.
[09:55] Avery Chen: before we close, any other concerns?
[10:00] Luis Ortega: one small ask — can Redwood share more detailed kernel selection logs? we want to map model perf to kernel variations.
[10:08] Marcus Bell: yes, we can export kernel id per inference and the exec path. i'll include that in the run outputs.
[10:14] Jin Soo: and please include tokenization diff for the failing prompts — that helped previously.
[10:19] Marcus Bell: good call.
[10:22] Nina Park: quick recap and owners: Marcus: 24h stability run + kernel logs by 2026-05-18; Nina: SOC2/ISO pack by 2026-05-16; Jin Soo: final prompt set and rubric by 2026-05-17; Sana/Maya: confirm success criteria and legal review by 2026-05-20; Avery: send detailed timeline for Private vs Dedicated by 2026-05-15.
[10:45] Avery Chen: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in thread with the artifacts and invite for 2026-05-26 rollback drill.
[10:52] [meeting end]

Notes on transcription: some product names got mangled in the automated transcript (e.g., "KV cache" occasionally transcribed as "K V cassette"), and participant labels may be slightly off in a few lines.

References shared: link: /redwood/pilot/edenware/scorecard.csv (internal), link: /redwood/security/soc2-bundle.zip (to be shared), spreadsheet: kernel-selection-traces-2026-05-14.csv (will be attached)
